A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PFT research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original PFT training experiments, phonon and thermal-conductivity evaluations, Matbench Discovery results, and appendix elasticity and energy-discrepancy analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations involving MACE, Nequix OAM, third-order force constants, computational efficiency, hyperparameter sensitivity and molecular-dynamics stability.

M1.justification: Equation (4), used in the EFS/PFT objective, changes the stated force loss from the mean squared L2 norm to the mean L2 norm. The sampled-column Hessian loss, HVP computation and co-training algorithm remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this is an implementation change or a formula correction.

E1.justification: v4 expands upstream training coverage beyond MPtrj by training Nequix OAM using OMat24 and subsampled Alexandria, incorporating substantially broader DFT configuration data. Appendix A.6 adds high-temperature molecular dynamics on five single-vacancy transition-metal systems from TM23, a distinct off-equilibrium test scenario. The existing phonon, conductivity, stability and elasticity coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v4 adds full-Hessian training as a direct comparator to stochastic HVP training in Appendix A.1 and introduces the stronger Nequix OAM reference in the main benchmarks. Table 1 adds displacement-only fine-tuning, previously compared only in Figure 3, and the PFT variant of MACE-MP-0. MACE-MP-0 itself and the original external baseline sets were already present.

E3.justification: v4 adds direct third-order force-constant MAE, five additional Matbench metrics, and protocols for OAM training, full-Hessian controls, backend benchmarking and 100-ps molecular dynamics. The reported PFT learning rate changes from 0.0003 to 0.0001, and the energy-comparison sample count changes from 9,959 to 9,868. These revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun. The original MDR test split and 95/5 training/validation division remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test stochastic HVP against full-Hessian training across three crystal symmetries, sensitivity to Hessian-loss weights of 10, 100 and 1000, molecular-dynamics stability, and PyTorch versus JAX computational costs. Additional architecture and pretraining-scale experiments examine generality. The original co-training ablation, energy-discrepancy analysis, elasticity evaluation and band-structure examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests or uncertainty estimates for the experimental results. The added experiments retain point estimates and training curves without introducing an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial results, including third-order MAEs of 10.52 versus 8.35 meV/Å³ for Nequix MP versus PFT, and OAM conductivity errors of 0.267 versus 0.198 before and after PFT. It also adds MACE, displacement-only, sensitivity, efficiency and MD findings. Existing Nequix MP PFT conductivity error changes from 0.306 to 0.307 and stability F1 from 0.747 to 0.748; these are reported numerical revisions, not established same-setting improvements. Retained Table 1 phonon scores and appendix elasticity scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (4) substantively revises the mathematical force-loss definition by removing the square on the L2 norm. The force-constant definitions, sampled-Hessian expectation and HVP identity remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about curvature supervision, scalable HVP training, co-training, 55% phonon improvement and transfer to third-order properties remain. The v4 introduction adds the claim that PFT also benefits a stronger OMat24-pretrained model despite substantially more upstream data, modestly broadening the explicitly demonstrated scope.

C2.justification: v4 explains the Hessian-loss-weight tradeoff between curvature accuracy and energy/force/stress accuracy, and clarifies that conductivity depends on both second- and third-order force constants. The discussion explicitly qualifies applicability by higher-order autodifferentiation availability and predominantly near-equilibrium evaluation, acknowledging that successful MD checks leave broader off-equilibrium evaluation unresolved.

D1.justification: v4 adds JAX and PyTorch HVP code, the OAM training recipe, FeNNol/OpenEquivariance implementation information, and specific model and GPU configurations. It newly states that training uses 8,510 structures derived from 301,414 displacement calculations. Reported PFT costs change from 140/60 to 35/15 A100-hours with/without co-training, without explaining the reduction. The stated code, weights and data access location is unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for OpenEquivariance, TM23, PyTorch and FeNNol, supporting the new implementations and experiments. Section 5 largely preserves the positioning relative to Hessian training, distillation and direct-Hessian prediction. The publication updates for Amin et al. and Fu et al. refer to existing cited works.

P1.justification: v4 corrects local grammatical errors, standardizes terminology and headings, and updates affiliation and conference text. It inserts a third-order-results subsection, additional appendix subsections and an Impact Statement. The abstract, contribution list and main background/method narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v4 substantially redesigns Figure 3 around a larger Hessian-error panel, updates plot palettes and captions, and adds three appendix figures covering efficiency, sensitivity and backend costs. It adds third-order and OAM-training tables, expands benchmark tables, and makes the Matbench table full-width with additional metric columns. Existing energy-discrepancy and appendix band plots are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important validation gaps in v1: direct third-order errors strengthen the transfer claim, MACE and OAM experiments test broader applicability, and full-Hessian controls substantiate computational advantages. Sensitivity analyses and implementation details also improve scrutiny and reproducibility. Unexplained loss/settings revisions and absent run-to-run uncertainty remain limitations, but the added evidence substantially strengthens the paper overall.
